checks.note: The itinerary covers exactly Day 1, Day 2 and Day 3, and the lodging estimate is for 2 nights, which matches.
Every day has named stops for breakfast, lunch, a snack or afternoon treat, and dinner. Sightseeing fits in around the meals.

Most dinners are $50–90 per person, and the cheap staples (bagels, Schwartz's, Chinatown, poutine) are balanced by one optional splurge. The total of about $800–1,200 per person is reasonably mid-range.
It covers fall foliage, 10–14°C highs, layers and a rain jacket, late-harvest apples and pumpkins at Jean-Talon, and foliage views from Mount Royal.

Almost everything is a named, real place: Olive et Gourmando, Schwartz's, St-Viateur, Fairmount, Au Pied de Cochon, Jean-Talon, Joe Beef, Damas, La Banquise and others. The weakest item is "Toqué!'s more casual sibling options", which is vague.

unasked_content: Day 1 lunch suggestion "Garde Manger or Toqué!'s more casual sibling options" doesn't name a place you can book. Garde Manger is also a pricier dinner spot, not a natural lunch stop.
Day 3 has a lot of backtracking: Chinatown, then Atwater/Saint-Henri, then La Banquise in the Plateau, then Joe Beef in Little Burgundy. It also puts a poutine stop right before the splurge dinner.
$80–120 per person likely underestimates Joe Beef with drinks, which makes the splurge look cheaper than it is.
Kem CoBa is a seasonal ice cream shop that may be closing or closed in October. The answer doesn't flag this, even though the trip is in October.
